critique.evidence: The dark grid, restrained cyan/magenta accents, oversized hero type, and consistent mono labels create a distinctive, polished defense-console aesthetic. Desktop has strong hierarchy and a well-composed atlas/detail split; mobile reflows the controls and detail panel coherently. However, the sticky global navigation visibly overlays the hero on desktop and cuts across the atlas controls on tablet, obscuring content and breaking the composition. Tablet also feels cramped and horizontally truncated, while mobile contains very small labels and a clipped code block that reduces legibility. These responsive defects keep it below genuinely demo-ready polish.
critique.fix: Correct sticky-header offsets and stacking so navigation never overlaps the hero or atlas card, especially at tablet width. Give tablet a deliberate stacked layout rather than a clipped desktop canvas, and make wide stage columns explicitly scrollable with clear affordance. On mobile, increase microtype slightly and wrap or horizontally scroll the JSON panel without hard clipping.
